# Warnings that already existed when this file was written, as `count<TAB>signature`.
# The check fails on anything not listed here, and on any signature occurring MORE
# times than its count -- normalization drops line numbers, so several warnings in
# one file can share a signature, and without the count a second instance of an
# already-listed warning would slip through.
#
# Shrinking this file is the point. Fix warnings, then --update-baseline
# --prune-baseline and land the smaller file.
#
# To shrink it, read which entries a CI run reports as no longer occurring and drop
# exactly those. A local run cannot distinguish a warning that was fixed from one
# that only ever appears on the build host, so --prune-baseline from a laptop will
# discard entries that are still real in CI.
#
# --update-baseline adds to this file rather than replacing it, because not every
# warning appears in every environment: SDK-header warnings surface on the build
# host but not always on a laptop. Replacing from a local run would drop those and
# fail CI on warnings nobody introduced. A local run reporting such an entry as
# 'no longer occurs' is expected and is not a failure.
